title.narrative: BGD BYETS

description.narrative: The Building Youth Employability through Skills (BYETS) is a 4-year long project supported by the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands (EKN) and implemented by Swisscontact. The project commenced in October 2022, intending to empower 25,000 Bangladeshi youth (including 50% women) with improved technical, employability, andentrepreneurial skills, and connect them to income-generating opportunities, namely, jobs and self-employment. BYETS will be working in 3 (three) sectors: Ready Made Garments (RMG), Agro- Processing (AP), and Information and Communication Technology (ICT).BYETS aims to partner with Training Service Providers (TSPs) and Employers to facilitate employment opportunities for youth across Dhaka,Chattogram, Khulna and Rajshahi in Bangladesh. BYETS will also support 50 private sector employers in the AP and RMG sectors to adopt Swisscontact’s proven workplace-based training (WBT) model.The interventions are expected to improve the capacity of Training Service Providers (TSPs) to deliver market-driven training and job placement services to job-seeking youth and enable them to offer customized entrepreneurship development support to youth seeking self-employment opportunities. Additionally, in partnership with private sector employers, the project will assist them in either improving existing WBT systems or setting up new ones within their enterprises to upskill and reskill existing workers, particularly women. BYETS will also embed content on labour rights and decent work (LRDW), gender equality and social inclusion (GESI), and Environmental Responsibility (ER) within the technical modules to develop youth’s capacity on transversal issues.

title.narrative: PSD Indicator J: Amount of mobilised private finance (in thousand EUR) Result

description.narrative: This figure represents the total contribution of partners across all sectors, encompassing both in-kind and cash contributions. This investment is ensured through multiple modalities, following OECD methodologies. This includes co-financing arrangements with implementing partners and direct investments by private sector employers or companies to facilitate the continuation of WBT within their premises. The training service provider partners' contribution is directly mentioned under the contract, and the investment of the factories is calculated using the cost per minute(CPM) method. The project collected CPM data from multiple factories within the BYETS portfolio of factories and calculated the average CPM for those factories. BYETS use this average to calculate the total investment by the factories for training sessions on their premises. For BYETS, CPM is calculated only for the manufacturing operations. Which includes the cost of salaries, rent, utilities, and any other costs.
